evaluation.production: Still profiles as a TE1 on a per-game basis, but the season median is deliberately held below a healthy-Kittle projection because of the Achilles return.
evaluation.ceiling: If the Achilles recovery holds and his route rate normalizes quickly, a top-five TE finish is still reachable.
evaluation.role: Clear starting tight end and one of the offense’s most important receiving pieces; role quality remains excellent when active.
evaluation.environment: Purdy/Shanahan and a concentrated passing game remain strong positives.
evaluation.availability: Torn right Achilles in January; activated from PUP on August 23 and returned only to individual work. Week 1 is possible, but early-season workload and re-injury risk must be priced in.
evaluation.reliability: Historically strong per-game scorer, but early 2026 weekly reliability is reduced until full-team work and normal snap volume return.
evaluation.sustainability: Efficiency and YAC history remain strong, but age 32 plus Achilles recovery makes peak-rate continuation less bankable.
evaluation.price: ADP around 92 is close to our target around 96, so he is fair rather than a clear value.

evaluation.production: 2025 was a real decline season, but the 2026 target path is materially cleaner than it was a year ago.
evaluation.ceiling: A return to strong red-zone volume can still produce a top-eight TE season even without a full efficiency rebound.
evaluation.role: Clear projected starter and Baltimore’s lone returning tight end; Likely’s departure materially improves route and target security.
evaluation.environment: Lamar Jackson and a high-scoring offense support touchdown upside, though the line has taken a hit with Danny Pinter expected to miss the season.
evaluation.availability: Age 30 but currently healthy; far less immediate availability concern than Kittle.
evaluation.reliability: The 2025 weekly floor was poor and late-season usage was inconsistent, so the model does not treat the role rebound as guaranteed.
evaluation.sustainability: Expect some rebound from 2025’s depressed yardage, but not a return to peak 2021 Andrews as the median.
evaluation.price: PPR ADP around 126 is well behind our target around 101, making him a value at current cost.

evaluation.production: The historical NFL production is modest, but 2026 volume can be much larger because the receiver depth chart has been stripped down.
evaluation.ceiling: If his strong camp translates into true No. 1/No. 2 target volume, he can beat a typical late-round WR ceiling by a wide margin.
evaluation.role: One of Miami’s top receivers in camp and repeatedly connecting with Malik Willis on explosive plays; a substantial role increase is justified.
evaluation.environment: The new quarterback, new offensive structure and pass-protection concerns cap efficiency expectations despite the open target tree.
evaluation.availability: Healthy entering the season with no major current availability penalty.
evaluation.reliability: He has never handled this kind of NFL receiving workload, so weekly consistency remains unproven.
evaluation.sustainability: The role opportunity is real, but we should not project alpha-WR efficiency from a player whose 2025 line was 46-317-3 receiving.
evaluation.price: Consensus PPR ADP around 224 is far behind our target around 132, making him a late-round value and upside bench target.
